bootstrap.title: Rust foundation, validated configuration, and cross-platform CI

decisions: RESP2 with binary keys and values; input limits and bounded channels since 0.1.
Storage with a single owner per worker; preserve boundaries between protocol, commands, storage, and networking.
Dataset quota rejects growth beyond the limit, without automatic eviction.
AOF initially uses a global writer, resolved mutation records, and a versioned format independent of the product version.
Shards remain fixed during execution; multi-key operations and transactions require the same shard and reject cross-shard access before any mutation.
Transactions distinguish queueing errors from execution errors as Redis does; individual errors during EXEC are not rolled back.
Asynchronous Sider→Sider replication, with the same version and shard configuration, a read-only replica, and manual promotion.
Compatibility is declared only with reproducible tests; responses without guaranteed ordering are compared by normalized content.
The supported environment through 1.0 is controlled; the default address remains on loopback.

0.2.0: SET with NX, XX, EX, PX, GET, and KEEPTTL

releases.title: RESP2 core
scope: Implement PING, ECHO, GET, basic SET, and DEL over RESP2/TCP, with a single worker.
Preserve binary data, fragmentation, per-connection ordering, limits, and shutdown as defined in PLANO.md.

tasks.title: Fixtures and Redis reference
tasks.objective: Pin a reproducible oracle for the five Sider 0.1 commands before implementing the codec.
deliverables: Literal RESP2 fixtures for PING, ECHO, GET, basic SET, and DEL, including arity errors.
Disposable infrastructure with Redis and redis-cli 8.10.1 using the image and digest recorded in reference; document reproducible manual execution.
tests: Check PONG bytes, nulls, empty values, and binary responses without reusing the future Sider decoder.
Verify reference version, digest, and availability; a missing tool must fail explicitly.
acceptance: Fixtures and reproduction commands are versioned; the matrix distinguishes intended contracts from support not yet implemented.

tasks.title: Incremental RESP2 codec
tasks.objective: Implement all five RESP2 types and incremental encoding/decoding independent of sockets and storage.
deliverables: Frame, RespLimits, atomic encoder, and decoder with a cursor/bounded stack as specified in PLANO.md.
The decoder preserves incomplete buffers, consumes one frame at a time, and limits bytes, nodes, and depth before allocating payloads.
tests: Round trips, every fragmentation point in short fixtures, byte-by-byte delivery, and concatenated frames.
Non-UTF-8 content, integer extremes, split CRLF, overflow, exact and exceeded limits; a work counter detects quadratic reprocessing.
acceptance: Codec tested without networking or a database, with no panic on arbitrary input; encoder errors leave no partial output.

tasks.title: Five commands and storage
tasks.objective: Implement parsing and synchronous execution of PING, ECHO, GET, basic SET, and DEL on binary keys and values.
deliverables: Command and Reply types, a state-independent parser, and a Store testable without a runtime.
Classify recoverable command errors and format errors; SET with options still returns ERR unsupported SET options without changes.
tests: Arity, ASCII command-name casing, missing and empty values, NUL, non-UTF-8 bytes, overwrites, and DEL with repeated keys.
Rejected commands preserve the map; DEL counts only actual removals.
acceptance: Semantics of all five commands verified by socket-free tests; error differences are recorded in the matrix.

tasks.title: Worker and TCP
tasks.objective: Connect the protocol to the owning worker through a bounded queue and oneshot responses, exposing a supervised TCP server.
deliverables: DbHandle, Request, and a worker that owns the Store; accept a command when enqueue completes and execute it even after client disconnection.
serve receives an already open listener; validated configuration, one in-flight request per connection, timeouts, limits, logs, and shutdown with bounded draining.
For the extracted binary smoke test, SIDER_ADDR accepts port 0 and SIDER_READY_FILE receives atomic JSON with pid, host, and port after bind; follow docs/releases.md.
tests: Ephemeral ports, SET/GET/DEL, two clients, concatenated commands, and ordered responses.
Backpressure with barriers, a slow client, half-close, truncated EOF, unavailable worker, cancellation, and shutdown during reading/queueing/writing.
acceptance: The binary serves TCP clients on loopback; resources and queues are bounded, and tests do not rely on fixed ports or sleeps to order actions.

tasks.title: Differential tests and robustness
tasks.objective: Demonstrate the 0.1 subset against Redis 8.10.1 and turn adversarial inputs into reproducible regressions.
deliverables: Differential suite independent of the codec under test and separate integration with redis-cli RESP2.
Robustness tests for truncated, concatenated, and malformed inputs; the runner produces compatibility gate evidence.
tests: Deterministic and generated sequences on disposable instances; compare bytes, response type, and observed state.
Cover limits, fragmentation, and rejections; convert findings into reproducible regressions.
acceptance: Five commands verified with redis-cli; the matrix identifies actual tests, limitations, and reference; a missing or ignored external test blocks delivery.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.1.0
acceptance: All R01 tasks completed with a PR and recorded manual verification; PING, ECHO, GET, basic SET, and DEL work through redis-cli.
native, compatibility, and tcp_smoke gates passed at the exact SHA; fragmentation, binary data, limits, and ordering covered.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: Strings, TTL, and memory
scope: Add EXISTS, INCR, DECR, MGET, MSET, EXPIRE, PEXPIRE, TTL, PTTL, and PERSIST.
SET accepts NX, XX, EX, PX, GET, and KEEPTTL; passive/active expiration and quota enforcement that rejects growth.

tasks.title: Additional string commands
tasks.objective: Extend strings with EXISTS, INCR, DECR, MGET, and MSET while preserving worker atomicity.
deliverables: Parsing, responses, and execution of all five commands with binary data and validation before mutation.
Document supported forms and count/byte limits applied to multi-key commands.
tests: i64 overflow, invalid integers, duplicates, missing keys, arity, and atomicity of rejected MSET.
Compare responses and state with Redis 8.10.1, including EXISTS multiplicity and MGET ordering.
acceptance: Additional commands pass native and differential tests; overflow and rejection do not corrupt state.

tasks.title: SET options
tasks.objective: Implement SET forms with NX, XX, EX, PX, GET, and KEEPTTL and finalize the combinations accepted by the subset.
deliverables: Parser validates combinations, arguments, and overflow before effects; represent the deadline/previous-value return in the resolved command.
Integrate timing options into the entry representation consumed by expiration in the next task; keep the stage buildable.
tests: Valid and incompatible combinations, zero/negative/excessive duration, previous value, missing key, and unmet condition.
Differential tests against Redis for the supported combination matrix; rejection preserves values and metadata.
acceptance: All declared SET forms have tests; no promise of complete expiration before R02-03.

tasks.title: Passive and active expiration
tasks.objective: Implement EXPIRE, PEXPIRE, TTL, PTTL, and PERSIST with expiration on access and bounded active cleanup.
deliverables: Injectable monotonic clock, expiration generations, and a bounded budget per cleanup round.
Integrate deadlines set by SET and distinguish missing, persistent, and expired keys; define future conversion to absolute deadlines for persistence.
tests: Controlled time without changing the global environment, exact expiration boundary, PERSIST, and updates before stale expiration.
Active expiration of unaccessed keys, repeated deletion/rewriting, and timing semantics compared with Redis using declared tolerances.
acceptance: A stale expiration event never deletes a new value; timed SET and all five TTL commands work with reads and active cleanup.

tasks.title: Dataset quota
tasks.objective: Limit accounted dataset growth with atomic rejection, without automatic eviction.
deliverables: Documented dataset memory configuration and accounting, distinct from RSS and network buffers.
Prevalidate growth in SET, MSET, and increments; release memory consistently on DEL, expiration, and smaller replacements.
tests: Exact/exceeded limit, larger/smaller replacement, partially admissible batch, and space recovery after expiration.
Rejected operations preserve data and counters; invalid configuration fails before opening the server.
acceptance: Growth above the quota is rejected without partial effects; accounting and differences are documented.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.2.0
acceptance: R01 milestone validated and R02 tasks completed; overflow, stale expiration, and rejections preserve state.
Local gates passed; quota rejects growth and SET/TTL options have differential evidence.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: AOF persistence
scope: AOF with a versioned format, checksum, and global writer of resolved mutations.
Explicit durability policies, safe replay, compaction, and crash tests on Linux and Windows.

tasks.title: Versioned AOF format and checksum
tasks.objective: Define and implement a durable format independent of product versions, capable of detecting truncation and corruption.
deliverables: Specification of header, version, record framing, checksum, and limits; records and batches contain resolved mutations and absolute deadlines.
Format reader/writer testable without a server and binary fixtures for the initial AOF version.
tests: Binary round trips, unknown size/version, incorrect checksum, overflow, and truncation at every record boundary.
The initial migration gate reads fixtures from the first format and explicitly rejects unknown versions.
acceptance: Initial format documented and reproducible; partial or invalid data does not become an applicable mutation.

tasks.title: Append and fsync
tasks.objective: Integrate a global AOF writer with explicit ordering between validation, logging, application, and response.
deliverables: Per-write and periodic fsync policies with documented acknowledgment guarantees.
Bounded channels, logging of resolved conditional operations, and append/fsync failure handling that prevents acknowledgment of durability not achieved.
tests: Injected failures in short writes, append, flush, and fsync; rejected commands do not enter the log as mutations.
Check response/log/state ordering and durable operations whose responses were lost.
acceptance: Each policy declares possible loss after a crash; success respects the selected guarantee and writer failure is supervised.

tasks.title: AOF recovery
tasks.objective: Recover persisted state before accepting connections, applying only complete and validated records.
deliverables: Deterministic replay with an explicit policy for truncated tails versus internal corruption, preserving the original file on error.
Reconstruct absolute TTL, quota, and metadata; recovery handles already expired entries.
tests: Restart after every log prefix, internal corruption, incomplete tail, clock change, and expiration during downtime.
Compare before/after state and verify that no partial record is applied.
acceptance: The recovery gate demonstrates the expected recovered state; corruption is not silently accepted and the listener opens only after successful recovery.

tasks.title: AOF compaction
tasks.objective: Compact the AOF while preserving concurrent mutations and replacing the file safely on each platform.
deliverables: Consistent snapshot of resolved mutations, bounded delta capture, and file replacement protocol with recoverable cleanup.
Documentation of replacement and file/directory synchronization guarantees applicable on Linux and Windows.
tests: Writes and expirations during compaction, disk failure, and interruptions before/after each replacement step.
Restart selects an intact file; compare state after compaction on both platforms.
acceptance: Compaction does not lose acknowledged mutations beyond the fsync policy; the original file remains recoverable until safe replacement.

tasks.title: Crash and durability tests
tasks.objective: Verify AOF guarantees with interrupted real processes and deterministic I/O failures.
deliverables: crash, recovery, and migration runners with reports tied to the SHA and durability policy.
Linux/Windows matrix of failures, timing, and permitted loss; preserve the regression file corpus.
tests: Terminate processes between append/fsync/response and during compaction; recover every resulting file.
Verify absence of partial mutations, adherence to per-write fsync, and the documented periodic policy limit.
acceptance: crash/recovery/migration gates execute real cases without counting ignored tests as success.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.3.0
acceptance: No partial record applied; fsync and recovery guarantees verified on Linux and Windows.
Local gates include crash, recovery, and migration; for the first AOF, migration uses initial-format fixtures.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: Shards
scope: Deterministic routing with hash tags and a fixed number of owning workers.
Multi-key operations require the same shard; AOF initially retains a global writer and recoverable ordering.

tasks.title: Stable routing and hash tags
tasks.objective: Define binary routing stable across operating systems and hash tags without claiming Redis Cluster support.
deliverables: Hash algorithm and tag extraction documented with test vectors; shard count validated at startup.
Router interface preserving the execution handle; configuration fixed for the lifetime of the process.
tests: Linux/Windows vectors, non-UTF-8 bytes, empty/nested tags, missing tags, and different shard counts.
acceptance: The same key and configuration always select the same shard on both platforms; online resharding remains out of scope.

tasks.title: Independent workers
tasks.objective: Partition storage among owning workers without direct concurrent sharing of maps.
deliverables: Bounded queue per worker and request routing; shutdown, TTL, and quota consistent with the partitioned configuration.
Worker supervision and an unavailability policy that rejects requests without functioning storage.
tests: Independent progress on different shards, a hot shard, queue saturation, and coordinated failure/shutdown.
acceptance: Each key has a single worker; per-connection order is preserved and backpressure remains bounded.

tasks.title: Restricted multi-key operations
tasks.objective: Validate all DEL, MGET, and MSET keys before sending an operation to the shard.
deliverables: Deterministic rejection of cross-shard operations before any effect.
Document the incompatibility introduced in minor version 0.4 and hash tag examples that preserve colocation.
tests: Same-shard batches, cross-shard batches, duplicates, missing keys, and binary bytes; compare complete state after rejection.
acceptance: No multi-key operation partially crosses shards; the restricted behavior appears in the matrix and notes.

tasks.title: Shard integration with AOF
tasks.objective: Keep replay and compaction consistent with multiple workers and a global AOF writer.
deliverables: Coordinate durable sequencing, checkpoints, and routing during recovery.
Validate shard metadata/configuration when opening AOF and provide an offline migration procedure when needed.
tests: Concurrent writes across shards, crashes, and compaction; recover the internal R03 AOF baseline identified by SHA and hashes, and compare state under a supported configuration.
acceptance: State and deadlines are preserved after recovery; incompatible configuration is detected before accepting clients.

tasks.title: Initial shard measurements
tasks.objective: Record partitioning costs and benefits with a reproducible workload, without an invented target for outperforming Redis.
deliverables: sharding runner and exploratory benchmark with configuration, hardware, seeds, and raw results.
Scenarios with different shard counts, hot keys, pipelines, and AOF enabled/disabled.
tests: Check data invariants under load and measure throughput, latency, and memory without mixing platforms/configurations.
acceptance: Distribution and correctness verified; reproducible results record bottlenecks, including potential global writer costs.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.4.0
acceptance: Same distribution on Linux and Windows; cross-shard rejection verified before any mutation.
AOF and migration preserve recovery; the sharding gate passes and initial measurements are recorded as local evidence.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: Basic collections
scope: Add typed hashes, lists, and sets with the command subset recorded in contracts.commands_added.
LPOP and RPOP initially omit count; preserve TTL, quota, AOF, and routing.

tasks.title: Typed values
tasks.objective: Evolve storage entries to explicit types and a uniform WRONGTYPE error.
deliverables: Representation of strings and collections with shared expiration and memory metadata.
Adapt existing commands to typed entries; AOF integration and reading of earlier data are completed in R05-05.
tests: Existing strings, type replacement by SET, WRONGTYPE without mutation, and replay of the previous format.
acceptance: Buildable typed foundation without claiming future commands; string behavior remains verified.

tasks.title: Hashes
tasks.objective: Implement HSET, HGET, HDEL, HEXISTS, HLEN, and HGETALL on binary fields and values.
deliverables: Parsing and execution of all six commands, counts of created/removed fields, and deletion of empty hashes.
Responses and metadata updates with arity and type validation before mutation.
tests: Repeated, empty, missing, and binary fields; WRONGTYPE and multi-field HSET.
Differential tests normalize HGETALL pairs without discarding field/value associations.
acceptance: Six hash commands tested and documented with responses, limits, and counting semantics.

tasks.title: Lists
tasks.objective: Implement LPUSH, RPUSH, LPOP, RPOP, LLEN, and LRANGE while preserving the order of binary elements.
deliverables: Pops without count, deletion of empty lists, and normalization of negative indices/ranges.
Integration with typed values and LRANGE response limits.
tests: Ordering of multiple pushes, missing/empty lists, negative/extreme indices, and extra pop arguments.
Differential tests preserve exact response ordering and check WRONGTYPE.
acceptance: Six list commands have differential and native cases; limits prevent partial responses or unintended mutation.

tasks.title: Sets
tasks.objective: Implement SADD, SREM, SISMEMBER, SCARD, and SMEMBERS with byte-based uniqueness.
deliverables: Set operations, counting only actual changes, and deletion of empty sets.
Differential comparison by normalized content for SMEMBERS, without promising iteration order.
tests: Duplicates, binary data, repeated removals, missing keys, cardinality, and WRONGTYPE.
acceptance: Five set commands demonstrate compatible uniqueness and counting semantics within the subset.

tasks.title: Collection integration with TTL, quota, and AOF
tasks.objective: Verify that all collections respect expiration, memory, and durability in single and batch operations.
deliverables: Growth accounting for new types, persistable resolved mutations, and collection replay/compaction.
types runner and per-type command matrix with evidence and limits.
tests: Quota rejecting a batch without partial effects, expiration after mutations, crashes, recovery, and migration from 0.4.
WRONGTYPE in each family and state equivalence after compaction.
acceptance: All types recover the same data and TTL; type and quota errors preserve state.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.5.0
acceptance: Hashes, lists, and sets have semantics, persistence, and WRONGTYPE verified per family.
types gate and local checks passed, including AOF migration and memory accounting.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: Sorted sets
scope: Add basic ZADD, ZREM, ZCARD, ZSCORE, and ZRANGE start stop [WITHSCORES].
Order by score and break ties by member bytes; retain persistence and limits.

tasks.title: Ordered storage
tasks.objective: Represent sorted sets with member lookup and consistent ordering by score and bytes.
deliverables: Structure with consistent updates and deletions across indexes; explicit rules for scores and tie-breaking.
Integration with typed entries, accounting, and expiration metadata.
tests: Repeated scores, score updates, non-UTF-8 bytes, removals, and index invariants under generated operations.
acceptance: A member appears once and both indexes agree; tie-breaking does not depend on locale or platform.

tasks.title: Basic sorted set commands
tasks.objective: Expose basic ZADD, ZREM, ZCARD, ZSCORE, and ZRANGE start stop [WITHSCORES] over RESP2.
deliverables: Score and range parsing with arity validation and explicit rejection of options outside the subset.
Score formatting and ordered responses compatible with the recorded reference.
tests: NaN/invalid scores, infinities according to the reference, negative and extreme indices, binary tie-breaking, and WITHSCORES.
Differential cases for updates, cardinality, missing values, duplicates, and WRONGTYPE.
acceptance: Five commands verified; rejections do not leave partial index updates.

tasks.title: Sorted set integration with persistence and limits
tasks.objective: Preserve scores, members, and ordering when applying quota, TTL, replay, and compaction.
deliverables: AOF logging and recovery of sorted sets, migration from the internal R05 baseline identified by SHA and hashes, and a sorted_sets runner.
Member/response/memory limit matrix and updated compatibility notes.
tests: Crash during updates, compaction, quota rejecting growth, and TTL; compare full ZRANGE before/after recovery.
acceptance: Recovery retains ordering and scores; indexes and memory remain consistent after failures and rejections.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.6.0
acceptance: Invalid scores handled, binary tie-breaking and negative indices verified.
sorted_sets gate and local checks passed; recovery preserves scores and ordering.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: Transactions
scope: Add MULTI, EXEC, DISCARD, WATCH, and UNWATCH restricted to one shard.
Separate queueing errors from individual execution errors without rollback; persist the batch atomically.

tasks.title: Per-connection transaction state
tasks.objective: Add MULTI, EXEC, and DISCARD as isolated connection state, with a bounded transaction queue.
deliverables: Active transaction state, queued commands, and queueing error; byte and command limits.
Parsing and QUEUED/error responses, cleanup on disconnection, and rejection of nested MULTI.
tests: Independent connections, EXEC/DISCARD without MULTI, errors before EXEC, limits, and disconnection with a pending queue.
acceptance: Queued commands do not change the database before EXEC; state is released on discard or disconnection.

tasks.title: Batch transaction execution
tasks.objective: Execute the entire batch in one worker, without interleaving external commands and with prior shard validation.
deliverables: Batch envelope and per-command responses; documented rule for transactions without keys.
Reject cross-shard access before effects; individual execution errors appear in the response and do not roll back other commands.
tests: Other clients cannot observe intermediate state; multi-shard transactions are rejected without effects.
Differential tests with queued arity errors, WRONGTYPE during EXEC, and valid commands before/after the error.
acceptance: Atomic execution within the shard and distinction between error classes verified; no promise of individual rollback.

tasks.title: WATCH and UNWATCH
tasks.objective: Implement optimistic concurrency control with watched key versions and invalidation by mutation or expiration.
deliverables: Per-connection bounded WATCH registry and cleanup on UNWATCH, EXEC, DISCARD, and disconnection.
Validate watches in the same worker that executes the batch, covering missing keys and expiration.
tests: Conflicts between clients, creation/removal of the same key, active/passive expiration, UNWATCH, and connection cleanup.
acceptance: Conflicts and expiration invalidate EXEC before any effect; old versions do not allow a stale transaction to commit.

tasks.title: Atomic batch persistence
tasks.objective: Ensure AOF applies all or none of the resolved mutations from an acknowledged EXEC, including responses with individual errors.
deliverables: Durable batch framing/checksum, atomic replay, and transaction-compatible compaction.
transactions runner, migration updates, and durability boundary documentation.
tests: Truncation at every batch boundary, crash during append/fsync/response, and replay with a previously resolved individual error.
Aborted WATCH and discarded EXEC do not produce mutation batches.
acceptance: Replay never applies a partial transaction; successful mutation order is preserved according to the durability policy.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.7.0
acceptance: Single-shard transactions, conflicts, and WATCH expiration verified; errors follow the declared Redis subset.
transactions gate and local checks passed; replay does not apply partial transactions.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: Pub/Sub
scope: Add SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, and PING in RESP2 subscriber mode.
Subscriptions and messages are ephemeral; bounded queues and slow clients do not block the database.

tasks.title: Subscription registry
tasks.objective: Create an ephemeral registry of binary channels and subscribers with explicit ownership and limits.
deliverables: Idempotent subscription/unsubscription, per-connection channel limit, and removal on shutdown.
Separate the Pub/Sub registry from persisted data and shard command queues.
tests: Binary/empty channels, repeated subscriptions, multiple subscribers, exact/exceeded limits, and release after disconnection.
acceptance: Consistent subscription counts and released memory; subscriptions do not reappear through AOF.

tasks.title: Message publication
tasks.objective: Implement PUBLISH to deliver binary messages to active subscribers and count recipients according to the contract.
deliverables: Distribution through bounded queues, publisher response, and RESP2 notification framing.
Document ephemeral delivery without replay and per-connection message ordering.
tests: Zero/one/multiple subscribers, binary and empty payloads, successive messages, and distribution without duplicates.
acceptance: Clients receive the expected bytes and ordering; PUBLISH does not write messages to the dataset/AOF.

tasks.title: Subscriber mode
tasks.objective: Integrate SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PING with RESP2 subscriber mode restrictions and responses.
deliverables: Transitions between normal and subscriber mode, per-channel acknowledgments, and mode exit after the last subscription.
Explicit matrix of allowed commands and transaction interactions.
tests: UNSUBSCRIBE without arguments, unknown channels, PING with/without a message, and commands disallowed in subscriber mode.
Differential tests of acknowledgments, counts, and messages against Redis 8.10.1.
acceptance: RESP2 responses and transitions verified; no mixing of command and notification framing.

tasks.title: Slow client handling
tasks.objective: Ensure subscribers that do not read cannot block publishers, storage, or other subscribers.
deliverables: Documented full-queue/timeout disconnection policy, per-connection limits, and centralized cleanup.
pubsub runner with bounded load testing and resource checks after reconnections.
tests: Slow subscriber with a small buffer, concurrent fast subscriber, concurrent publication, timeout, and shutdown.
acceptance: The database remains responsive, queues never grow without bounds, and disconnection removes all subscriptions.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.8.0
acceptance: Slow subscribers do not block the database or healthy subscribers; bounded queues and cleanup verified.
pubsub gate and local checks passed, including PING behavior in subscriber mode.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: Replication
scope: Asynchronous Sider→Sider replication with the same version and shard configuration.
Full and incremental synchronization, reconnection, read-only replicas, and manual promotion; no automatic failover.

tasks.title: Versioned internal protocol
tasks.objective: Define internal replication transport with identity, version, sequence, and resource limits.
deliverables: Handshake validating the Sider version, replication format, and shard configuration.
Versioned, bounded snapshot, resolved mutation, and transaction batch messages; replica rejects client writes.
tests: Incompatible version/configuration, partial/malformed messages, overflow, lost connection, and attempted writes on the replica.
acceptance: Incompatibility is rejected before applying state; the protocol does not claim compatibility with Redis replication.

tasks.title: Full synchronization
tasks.objective: Transfer a cross-shard consistent snapshot with a sequence position that allows subsequent mutations to be followed.
deliverables: Coordinated state capture, bounded transfer, and installation that exposes only complete snapshots.
Preserve all types, absolute deadlines, and batches; handle temporary files on failure/restart.
tests: Writes and expirations during snapshots, interruptions mid-transfer, and empty replicas/replicas with previous state.
acceptance: Replica never exposes a partial mixture of snapshots; data from every shard corresponds to the declared consistent point.

tasks.title: Incremental replication
tasks.objective: Apply mutations after the snapshot in a continuous sequence with a bounded backlog.
deliverables: Bounded replication history, position acknowledgments, and ordered application of resolved mutations.
Preserve TTL and batch atomicity; document asynchronous replication and possible loss on promotion.
tests: Duplicates, gaps and incorrect sequences, transactions with individual errors, expiration, and multiple replicas at different speeds.
acceptance: State converges with the primary after catching up to the sequence; no partial transaction becomes visible.

tasks.title: Replica reconnection
tasks.objective: Resume replication from available history or request a new full synchronization with explicit fallback.
deliverables: Resumption verified by stream identity/epoch and position, bounded backoff, and old connection cleanup.
Insufficient history or changed identity forces full synchronization, without claiming continuity.
tests: Short/long disconnection, exceeded backlog, primary/replica restart, and failures during resynchronization.
acceptance: Reconnection neither duplicates nor skips mutations; missing history always produces verifiable resynchronization.

tasks.title: Manual promotion
tasks.objective: Allow explicit replica promotion and document role changes without automatic failover.
deliverables: Administrative promotion operation with identity/epoch transition and disconnection from the old upstream.
Recovery procedure and prevention of unintended reconnection; the replication runner records consistency and lag.
tests: Promotion of caught-up and lagging replicas, writes after promotion, upstream reappearance, and restart of the new primary.
acceptance: Promotion is manual and observable; asynchronous loss limit is explicit and the replica remains read-only until transition.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.9.0
acceptance: Consistent synchronization across shards, read-only replicas, TTL and transactions preserved.
replication gate and local checks passed; insufficient backlog forces full synchronization and promotion is manual.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: Operations and distribution
scope: Metrics, diagnostics, and reproducible backup and restore procedures.
Distribute a Linux amd64 Docker image as an archive attached to the private release; verify operation and shutdown.

tasks.title: Metrics
tasks.objective: Expose verifiable operational metrics without logging user keys, values, or channels.
deliverables: Counters/gauges for connections, commands, errors, and queues; instrument dataset, expiration, AOF, and replication lag as each subsystem is integrated, with full coverage verified in R10-05.
Read contract, units, and bounded cardinality; configuration and documentation of exposure in the controlled environment.
tests: Known load produces expected counts, concurrency does not lose updates, and labels do not grow per key/channel.
acceptance: Metrics have definitions and tests; no user data in labels or RSS claims derived from logical quota.

tasks.title: Operational diagnostics
tasks.objective: Enable diagnosis of configuration, saturation, and persistence/replication failures with actionable information.
deliverables: Administrative output of version and nonsensitive effective configuration; integrate replication role and AOF state when available, with full coverage verified in R10-05.
Runbook for full queues, unavailable disks, slow clients, and replica lag with logs of relevant events.
tests: Injected failures produce consistent diagnostics and appropriate exit codes; output does not expose client payloads.
acceptance: The operator identifies state and cause without inferring internal implementation; diagnostics match metrics.

tasks.title: Backup and restore procedures
tasks.objective: Provide a tested procedure to capture a consistent backup and restore a Sider instance.
deliverables: Backup guide with a consistent point, checksums, version/format/configuration, and TTL preservation.
Automated restore procedure in an isolated directory and instance, without overwriting a dataset in use.
tests: Backup under traffic, restore of types/transactions/shards, and state comparison; corrupted archives or incompatible configuration fail explicitly.
acceptance: Reproducible restore from the distributed archive, accounting for elapsed TTL time and durability limits.

tasks.title: Docker image
tasks.objective: Package Sider Linux amd64 in a runnable image and validate its archive export for the private 1.0 publication.
deliverables: Reproducible Dockerfile with version/SHA, unprivileged user, persistent directory, and correct stop signal.
Build, compressed docker save, checksum, and release manifest inclusion; the docker runner tests the exported image after load.
tests: --version, TCP smoke, volume persistence, restart, invalid configuration, and container shutdown.
acceptance: Exported and reloaded image runs the tests; distribution neither depends on a public registry nor exposes the repository.

tasks.title: Operational tests
tasks.objective: Validate complete operation with documented limits and procedures using distributed artifacts.
deliverables: Startup, saturation, disk failure, backup/restore, replication, and shutdown tests in supported environments.
Report with commands, artifacts, configuration, results, and controlled environment limitations.
tests: Packages extracted on Linux/Windows and reloaded image; test signals, draining, resumption, and metrics during failures.
acceptance: Documentation reproduces results; metrics, restore, and shutdown verified across distribution channels.

gate.title: Validate internal milestone 0.10.0
acceptance: Metrics verified, restore reproducible, shutdown and limits documented.
docker gate and local checks passed; the exported runnable image accompanies the private packages and checksums.
Verify technical criteria and record local evidence; close this internal milestone without a candidate, tag, or published release. Artifacts used in migration remain frozen by SHA and hashes.

releases.title: Stabilization
scope: Freeze the compatible subset, verify recovery and migration, and run sustained load tests and reproducible benchmarks.
Include sorted sets, transactions, and Sider→Sider replication; document guarantees without promising out-of-scope capabilities.

tasks.title: Subset freeze
tasks.objective: Finalize the 1.0 contract for commands, protocol, persistence, operations, and replication with an explicit support matrix.
deliverables: Complete matrix with command form, limitation, reference version, and supporting test.
Post-1.0 compatibility policy and per-configuration durability guarantees; explicit list of later features.
tests: Review each claim against a test/report and identify gaps as blockers, without converting planned items into verified support.
acceptance: No unverified capability appears as supported; every item in the 1.0 subset has planned evidence and an owner.

tasks.title: Differential audit
tasks.objective: Audit the entire Redis subset with varied sequences and independent protocol and state comparison.
deliverables: Per-family corpus and cross-family sequences of types, TTL, transactions, and Pub/Sub with reproducible seeds.
Report distinguishing intentional differences from defects, with regressions for every corrected finding.
tests: Redis/CLI 8.10.1 pinned; normalize only responses without guaranteed ordering, without masking scores, pairs, or list order.
Arity, binary data, missing values, rejections, limits, and recoverable failures in every supported form.
acceptance: Audit passes without undeclared differences; the matrix links every supported form to results.

tasks.title: Sustained load tests
tasks.objective: Detect corruption, leaks, and progress issues under sustained load and combined failures.
deliverables: soak runner lasting at least 3600 seconds, with recorded dataset/seed/configuration and continuous invariant checks.
Disconnection, TTL, AOF/compaction, transaction, slow subscriber, and replication scenarios with resource monitoring.
tests: One hour of continuous load without unexplained failures; collect memory, queue, error, and progress measurements.
Crash/recovery and regressions for all findings in each candidate.
acceptance: No known corruption or loss beyond declared guarantees; the report distinguishes OOM/configuration issues from product defects.

tasks.title: Migration from the internal R10 baseline
tasks.objective: Demonstrate upgrading the internal R10 baseline, frozen by SHA and hashes, to 1.0 while preserving the dataset and persistence contracts.
deliverables: Backup, shutdown, upgrade, and verification procedure; backup restoration strategy if needed.
Internal R10 baseline fixtures and executables used in the migration gate, with SHA, metadata, and hashes.
tests: Create data of all types using the frozen internal R10 baseline executable, include TTL and transactions, upgrade, and verify state/recovery.
Supported shard configurations, damaged archive, expiration during downtime, and replica recreation under the same-version contract.
acceptance: Reproducible migration from the internal R10 baseline to 1.0 documented; no promise of replication between different versions.

tasks.title: Benchmarks and final documentation
tasks.objective: Publish reproducible results and sufficient documentation to install, operate, and evaluate Sider 1.0.
deliverables: benchmarks runner with throughput, p50/p95/p99, and memory, covering pipelines, hot keys, and different shard counts.
Raw results, hardware/toolchain/configuration, installation/operation/recovery guides, and final limitation notes.
tests: Rerun documented commands using extracted packages and the exported image; verify metrics and units.
Comparisons, when present, use declared conditions and do not turn an exploratory benchmark into a performance guarantee.
acceptance: Reproducible benchmarks without an artificial threshold for outperforming Redis; final documentation matches the 1.0 artifact and evidence.

gate.title: Validate and publish 1.0.0
acceptance: Sorted sets, transactions, and replication included; complete matrix without known corruption or loss beyond declared guarantees.
All gates passed, including a 3600-second soak, migration from the internal R10 baseline identified by SHA and hashes, and benchmarks.

Candidate approved with an immutable SHA and bundle; the final release promotes the same files and SHA without rebuilding. Any bundle change requires another candidate; close the milestone after verifying final publication.
